title: Intelligence Data and Software Engineer (MGySgt to LCpl) NMOS (0231, 0241, 0261, 2621, 2629, 2631, 2641, 2651, 2659), DIR INTEL
raw_text:
10. MOS 2652, Intelligence Data and Software Engineer (MGySgt to LCpl) NMOS
(0231, 0241, 0261, 2621, 2629, 2631, 2641, 2651, 2659), DIR INTEL

    a. Summary. The Intelligence Data and Software Engineer is a data and
database specialist that supports the Marine Corps Intelligence Surveillance
Reconnaissance Enterprise to streamline the intelligence production chain,
and designing, developing, and enabling software-based solutions to
intelligence challenges across the enterprise, to include knowledge
management, skill management, user applications, and research advanced data
and cybersecurity strategies, apply a secure coding standard in accordance
with national intelligence policy, across multiple classification domains.
Marines will work with multiple types of databases to capture and process
live, streaming, and distributed data, to include designing and developing
customized data collection, management, and search-and-retrieval systems to
support the collection, processing, exploitation, analysis, and dissemination
of datasets. Marines will work with several programming languages to address
user-specific visualization needs that accelerate intelligence data
processing for immediate-to-instant intelligence services. They employ
modern computation technologies that support the use of data science and
artificial intelligence tools, enabled by their skills in SQL, PowerShell,
Python, R, C, C++, java, JavaScript, and HTML programming languages. They
are also primarily responsible for the execution of Data Intelligence
operations and Data Intelligence reporting to automate and enhance the
intelligence production cycle.

       b.   Prerequisites

        (1) Must currently hold PMOS 0231, 0241, 0261, 2621, 2629, 2631,
2641, or 2651.

        (2) Security requirement: must have a current single scope
background investigation/TS investigation and adjudicated for sensitive
compartmented information (SCI) eligibility.




                                          3-165                      Enclosure (1)
 3122                                                                NAVMC 1200.1L



    c. Requirements.        Complete the Intelligence Data Engineer Capstone
Course (N46C1F2).

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to (p),
Signal Intelligence Training and Readiness Manual, Marine Corps Cyberspace
Operations (MCIP 3-40.02).

       e.   Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code

        (1) Reference the Marines Corps Credentialing Opportunities On-line
(COOL) Program.

            (2) United Services Military Apprenticeship Program (USMAP).

       f.   Related Military Skill

            (1) Intelligence Specialist, 0231.

            (2) Intelligence Analyst, 0239.

            (3) Geographic Intelligence Specialist, 0261.

            (4) Application Developer, 0673.

            (5) COMINT/EW Operator, 2621.

            (6) SIGINT/EW/CO Technician, 2629.

            (7) ISR Systems Engineer, 2651.
common_text: CYCBERSPACE OPERATIONS 1. Introduction. The Signals Intelligence (SIGINT), Electromagnetic Warfare (EW) OccFld includes the employment of SIGINT, EW, support to cyberspace operations (CO) and intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) systems engineering capabilities. Marines in this field are required to set up and operate collection and communications electronic equipment, manage intelligence data, prepare EW and intelligence reports, extend and mesh intelligence services, conduct preventive maintenance on assigned equipment, execute electromagnetic attack (EA), and assist in the operational control and management of SIGINT/EW/CO personnel, equipment, and facilities. Entry- level jobs include Communications Intelligence/Electromagnetic Warfare Operator, Signals Intelligence/Electromagnetic Warfare Analyst, Intelligence Surveillance Reconnaissance Systems Engineer, and Cryptologic Language Analyst. Marines can LATMOV into the 2600 OccFld at the grade of corporal or sergeant. Sergeants requesting LATMOV into the 2600 OccFld must have no more than 1 year time in grade. Duty assignments include Marine Forces Special Operations Command (MARSOC), Marine Corps Information Command (MCIC), Marine Forces Cyber Command (MARFORCYBER), Marine Cryptologic Support Battalion (MCSB), radio battalions, intelligence battalions, infantry battalions, littoral combat team (LCT), marine littoral regiments (MLR), and the staff sections of the MEF information groups (MIG), Marine divisions (MARDIV), and Marine aviation wings (MAW).

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
